paper.title_en: Anisotropic separate universe : Long-wavelength perturbations and conserved quantities
paper.abstract_en: We study the superhorizon evolution of linear perturbations in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe with a scalar field coupled to a U(1) gauge field. The analysis employs the spatial gradient expansion in the uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ gauge, in which the local number of $e$-folds is unperturbed. In this gauge, the complete set of leading-order long-wavelength solutions, including both even- and odd-parity perturbations, can be constructed from variations of homogeneous Bianchi type I solutions, subject to the momentum and Gauss constraints. The conserved Wronskian found in isotropic multi-field inflation is generalized to the anisotropic system. Together with the shear and electric-flux integration constants, it allows the curvature perturbation on uniform-$\mathcal{N}$ hypersurfaces to be expressed in terms of background variations and time integrals. The conserved comoving curvature perturbations are then obtained by adding this intrinsic curvature contribution to the familiar $δN$ contribution arising from the change of time slicing. We also derive a relation between the curvature perturbation and a metric perturbation that reduces to the plus-polarized tensor mode in the isotropic limit, and discuss a nonlinear extension of the formalism.
